help.check/assignment-to-immutable: Declare it with `var` to change it later.
help.check/captured-variable: Pass the value in as a parameter, or write a named `fn` inside this one, which may use it.
help.check/endless-type: Make the field that recurs optional (`next: Node?`) or a list (`kids: Node[]`), or add a leaf alternative.
help.check/exhaustiveness: Name every alternative of a choice, or end a match on a scalar with `case _ { ... }`.
help.check/finish: `finish CALL` ends the workflow with CALL's result, so CALL gives the workflow's own type; at least one branch goes on, and a `for` step never finishes.
help.check/inference-failure: Give the binding a type, `let x: Item = {...}`, or build the record by name, `Item(name: "pen")`.
help.check/match-type-mismatch: Match on a scalar or a choice; for an optional, test `x.exists()` and use `x` inside.
help.check/missing-field: Set every field the record declares, or give the field a default in the record.
help.check/missing-return: A step block ends with `return <name>`, naming the value it made.
help.check/record-context: Build the record by name, `Item(name: "pen")`, or give the binding a type.
help.check/recursion-limit: A recursive function says how deep it may go: `fn walk(n: Node) -> Number recurse 32 { ... }`.
help.check/return-outside-function: Workflows have no `return`: their last step's value is the result.
help.check/unknown-method: Each type has a fixed set of methods (KOSIKA.md lists them); to map a list, write `for x in xs { ... }`.
help.engine/not-yet: Write it without that feature, or run the program on the engine that reads it (`kosika`).
help.lex/unexpected-character: Kosika writes `and`, `or` and `not` where other languages write `&&`, `||` and `!`; the message quotes the character it stopped at.
help.parse/if-step-else: Write `name = if COND { CALL } else { CALL }`: both ways give the step a value, or one may `finish` the workflow.
help.parse/step-call: A workflow step is one line `name = <one call>`; put other logic in a `fn` and call it.
help.parse/workflow-item: A workflow holds steps (`name = <one call>`), `parallel { }`, `require approval` and `budget`; put logic in a `fn`.
